subject: Even talking about pollution is dangerous
alt: Kamal Kishore's cartoon: on the left an elderly woman with white hair and glasses stands in a pink sari, a blue mask over her face, looking ahead. Facing her stands a balding elderly man in a white shirt and grey trousers, also in a blue mask. At the upper left her speech bubble reads: pollution is dangerous.. In the middle a larger bubble, his, reads: talking about pollution is even more dangerous! At the upper right a box like a newspaper cutting reads: crackers raised pollution... On the right, in a hazy grey room, black rings of smoke curl upward.
chutki: The elderly woman says: pollution is dangerous.. and the elderly man facing her replies: talking about pollution is even more dangerous! Both wear masks, and above them a newspaper cutting warns that firecrackers raised pollution.

The cartoon's real point is that the danger is no longer only in the air but in speaking about it. When breath runs short after Diwali night, it is the one who asks the question who is put in trouble; the masks are on both faces, but the silence has become one person's need.
